conclusions.conclusion: READ COMMITTED is required before locks. VOLATILE PL/pgSQL uses separately executed statements and invokes the existing strict STABLE fence projection after the root lock. No combined pre-wait snapshot, split connection or exception block releasing locks appears. Existing immediate account_security parent FK provides the intended KEY SHARE conflict. PostgreSQL race scheduling and both winner paths remain root runtime obligations; future native writers must preserve FK and lock order.

conclusions.evidence: identity adapter guard call before UPDATE; with_audits transaction error/commit branches; strict FENCE_BODY unchanged
conclusions.conclusion: Missing routine/table/root, unavailable authority, SQL cancellation/error, null result and unsupported isolation propagate as errors before or within the same transaction, with no false legacy default. SQLx bool decoding rejects null. Only exact guard P0002+subject_not_found maps to existing Domain(NotFound). Backend death rolls back transaction in PostgreSQL; bounded cleanup/cancellation proof is not inferred from source. Altering the guard STABLE would make its SELECT FOR UPDATE impermissible; this source observation is not a runtime result.

conclusions.conclusion: Any security row preserves Account custody regardless of state. Fenced transition omits both auth revoke events, reports truthful operation revoke counts zero and preserves Company transition/archive/session-generation behavior. Fenced inactive replay holds locks, commits no credential changes/audits, then returns existing typed Conflict. Unfenced transition/replay retain original credential sweep, audit event order, racing-credential cleanup and typed outcomes. Entire sweep helper and other methods are byte-identical.

conclusions.conclusion: New routine is uniquely named/exact two UUID args/boolean, PL/pgSQL VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER, owner console_account_owner, fixed pg_catalog,pg_temp search_path, exact body/options and only two nongrantable EXECUTE entries (owner and console_rt). Existing owner topology disallows LOGIN/BYPASS/inheritance/membership. Owner users rights are only SELECT(id,org_id), UPDATE(id), nongrantable with users-owner grantor; PUBLIC/broad effective table or column rights, MAINTAIN, unexpected rights and grant options refuse. Existing six routine bodies, root/account ACL contracts and legacy credential ACLs are unchanged.

conclusions.evidence: generator generated_files control flow; unchanged INSTALL/ROOT_INSTALL blocks; generated SQL equality
conclusions.conclusion: Installer validates full profile under users-first seven table locks before inspecting certified root presence. Present corrupt routine/grants refuse. Absent guard plus dormant extension on valid roots enters only DEACTIVATION_INSTALL; old install/backfill blocks are skipped. Missing roots refuse. Complete finalized replay returns before mutation. Historical rootless inputs retain old path then receive the guard. Final full-profile certification occurs within one atomic DO; failure aborts installation rather than repairing drift.

Startup admits only account_custody.finalized; missing/corrupt mandatory guard produces an upgrade or drift status and refuses. No per-operation full metadata fingerprinting added. Arbitrary privileged post-startup routine-body replacement is outside the accepted trust boundary and demonstrated coverage; this does not excuse installer/startup drift checks.

compatibility_finding.evidence: Both suites use #[sqlx::test(migrations="../../platform/db/migrations")] and raw SET ROLE console_rt pool helpers, with no custody preparation/finalization call. cargo_needs_postgres.sh creates the isolated topology and runs mapped Cargo tests; no per-test Account finalizer is injected.
compatibility_finding.impact: The newly mandatory guard is absent in those test databases, so retained direct deactivation calls would fail42883 before their existing assertions. This is a source-grounded fixture compatibility issue, not a measured runtime failure and not grounds to weaken the product guard.
compatibility_finding.resolution: Root explicitly authorized Inventory to prepare a separate minimal private fixture prerequisite patch, preserving every existing case/assertion. That patch requires its own exact independent review and runtime. Product V1 remains frozen.
